title: Ops Signal Fabric — weekly sketch: GPU capacity & regional priming
body:
Purpose:
Quick, informal capture from the weekly ops huddle on the ‘signal fabric’ approach — stitching regional capacity signals, soft-reserves, and priming lanes to reduce coldstarts and mitigate regional pressure spikes. This is a sketch/notebook for the team; still many open questions and TODOs.

TL;DR:
- Short-term: enable soft-reserve in eu-west and apac for the next 72h window to bring spare capacity target from measured 7.4% -> target 12% during peak forecast.
- Mid-term: attempt mosaic-slot multiplexing prototype (experiment infra-mux-17) for heterogeneous GPUs to reduce fragmentation by ~6–10%.
- Risks: prewarming costs vs user latency improvements need guardrails; set a daily cap.

Observations this week:
1) Regional signal deltas
  - us-west: healthy, avg spare 11.8% midday, but 5 spikes where preemption + scheduled maintenance overlapped (tickets INFRA-4312, INFRA-4316).
  - eu-west: steady decline in evenings; recent tenant onboarding consumed small-slot pools. Spare now ~6.1% at 18:00 UTC.
  - apac (sin): highest variance, coldstart tail longer (~220ms p50->p95 delta), prewarming reducing tail but adding cost.

2) Priming lanes experiment (priming-lane-v3)
  - Setup: 3 warmers per AZ, lightweight prefix cache seeded from last-hour KV snapshots.
  - Result: median coldstart reduced ~38ms in us-west in early tests; cost overhead ~0.9% of daily GPU cycles.
  - Notes: effectiveness drops on long-tail sequences (>1024 tokens) — need dynamic warmers tied to seq-length distribution.

3) Mosaic slot multiplexing (infra-mux-17 prototype)
  - Goal: reduce slot fragmentation when mixing a100/rtx-capacity in same pool.
  - Early sim: theoretical ~8% better packing for typical chat workloads (short + bursty).
  - Next: small canary to 2-edge-racks in eu-west; measure scheduling latency and OOM signals.

Action items (owner — due):
- Asha: flip soft-reserve on in eu-west for 72h window and tune cap to 10% (2026-04-08).
- Diego: deploy mosaic-mux canary to eu-west edge racks, capture slot-packing metrics (2026-04-10).
- Riley: add sequence-length bucket to priming-lane controller and run ablation (2026-04-12).
- Marcus: draft short-lived cost guardrail policy for prewarming (daily budget, kill-switch) and circulate to SRE/product (2026-04-09).

Open questions / discussion points:
- What’s acceptable daily spend for prewarming vs SLA uplift? Product input needed — assign PO.
- How to signal downstream billing/console when soft-reserve is active (visibility for customers on Dedicated)?
- Should we bind priming lanes to customer tiers (only enterprise + high-SLO routes)?

Notes from standup chatter (shorthand):
- "quiet windows" help reduce noise for priming — add a scheduler window 02:00-04:00 UTC for heavy priming ops.
- Avoid priming on racks with heavy spot eviction history.
- Consider short TTL for seeded KV caches (30m) to avoid stale prefixes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Cost creep: mitigation = daily budget + auto-disable at threshold + Slack alert channel (#infra-priming-alerts).
- Regression in p95 latency if warmers misbehave: mitigation = canary + gradual rollout + fallback to no-warmers.
- Scheduling instability from mosaic mux: mitigation = tight telemetry, OOM thresholds, immediate revert playbook.

Metrics to track (dashboard calls needed):
- regional-spare-percent (per-AZ) — current baseline: us-west 11.8%, eu-west 6.1%, apac 7.4%
- coldstart-tail (p95) pre/post priming per region
- slot-fragmentation index (new metric from infra-mux sim)
- prewarming-cost-per-day (USD) and % of GPU cycles

Meeting artifacts / links:
- priming-lane-v3 experiment notes: https://confluence.redwood/priming-lane-v3
- infra-mux-17 sim results: https://githu b.com/redwood-inference/infra-sims/infra-mux-17 (PR pending)
- related Jira: JIRA-INFRA-4312, JIRA-INFRA-4326

Quick decisions for next week:
- Approve soft-reserve in eu-west (Asha to execute).
- Run mosaic-mux canary in eu-west only until 2026-04-16.
- Gather product input on acceptable priming budget (Marcus to ping PO).

If you’re reading this and want to push changes — edit inline, add comments, or ping me in #infra-signal-fabric. Keep notes terse; this is a sketch, not a polished playbook.
